# technitium_record_mx (Resource)

Manages a single `MX` record in an authoritative zone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_zone" "mx_home" {
  zone = "mx.example.com"
}

resource "technitium_record_mx" "mail" {
  zone       = technitium_zone.mx_home.zone
  domain     = technitium_zone.mx_home.zone
  exchange   = "mail.mx.example.com"
  preference = 10
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The record's domain name, for example `www.example.com`. Use the zone name for a record at the zone apex.
- `exchange` (String) The mail server's domain name.
- `preference` (Number) The mail server's preference. Lower values are tried first.
- `zone` (String) The authoritative zone that holds the record.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Comments stored with the record.
- `disable` (Boolean) Disable the record without deleting it. Defaults to `false`.
- `expiry_ttl` (Number) Deletes the record automatically this many seconds after it was last modified. Terraform then creates it again on the next apply. Defaults to `0`, which keeps the record.
- `ttl` (Number) The record TTL in seconds. Defaults to the default record TTL in the server settings.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# zone/domain/exchange/preference
terraform import technitium_record_mx.mail mx.example.com/mx.example.com/mail.mx.example.com/10
```
